svg.title: Base-Case Gross Proceeds to Owner Net
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-profit-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: Base-Case Gross Proceeds to Owner Net; subtitle: $1,025,000 annual gross equipment resale proceeds → $164,000 annual owner net.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: USD per year. First and last bars are absolute totals; the middle four bars are signed deductions. Acquisition, refurbishment, and delivery are modeled direct costs, separate from operating overhead. The cost allocation is illustrative; canonical revenue, net margin, and owner net are fixed. No unlisted residual deduction is assumed.; caption: $1,025,000 − $574,000 − $102,500 − $41,000 − $143,500 = $164,000, exactly 16.0% of gross resale proceeds. Gross proceeds are operator equipment sales, not a brokerage fee or the buyer's downstream clinical receipts.; stages: label: Gross resale proceeds; value: $1,025,000 | Opening total, 100.0%; numeric value: 1025000.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case annual equipment resale revenue. Recognize sales under the operator's applicable accounting policy; exclude pass-through sales taxes and refundable deposits from this illustrative revenue total.; label: Equipment acquisition; value: −$574,000 | 56.0% of gross proceeds; numeric value: -574000.0; detail: Cost of equipment sold, including purchase premiums assigned to those units; remaining bridge value is $451,000. Unsold purchases stay in inventory rather than becoming current-period cost of sold equipment.; label: Refurbishment and biomed QA; value: −$102,500 | 10.0% of gross proceeds; numeric value: -102500.0; detail: Parts, direct contractor bench labor, calibration, documented decontamination, and unit-level testing assigned to sold units; remaining bridge value is $348,500. Do not charge the same contractor invoice again within overhead.; label: Delivery and transaction costs; value: −$41,000 | 4.0% of gross proceeds; numeric value: -41000.0; detail: Crating, insured freight, payment charges, and modeled sale-related warranty expense; remaining bridge value is $307,500. Assign warranty exposure consistently and avoid counting both the provision and settlement as separate costs.; label: Pod and operating overhead; value: −$143,500 | 14.0% of gross proceeds; numeric value: -143500.0; detail: Loaded payroll, premises, insurance, software, selling expense, and administration consume $143,500 annually, approximately $11,958 monthly within the $4,000–$18,000 canonical operating range. This is a budget envelope requiring local staffing validation.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $164,000 | Closing total, 16.0%; numeric value: 164000.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case modeled owner net, with no additional deduction invented for an unspecified tax or funding structure. Reference scenarios remain $250,000 × 10% = $25,000 and $1,800,000 × 22% = $396,000; owner net is not gross margin.

text.title: Base-Case Gross Proceeds to Owner Net
text.tspan: Base-Case Gross Proceeds to Owner Net

circle.title: label: Gross resale proceeds; value: $1,025,000 | Opening total, 100.0%; numeric value: 1025000.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case annual equipment resale revenue. Recognize sales under the operator's applicable accounting policy; exclude pass-through sales taxes and refundable deposits from this illustrative revenue total.

label: Equipment acquisition; value: −$574,000 | 56.0% of gross proceeds; numeric value: -574000.0; detail: Cost of equipment sold, including purchase premiums assigned to those units; remaining bridge value is $451,000. Unsold purchases stay in inventory rather than becoming current-period cost of sold equipment.

label: Refurbishment and biomed QA; value: −$102,500 | 10.0% of gross proceeds; numeric value: -102500.0; detail: Parts, direct contractor bench labor, calibration, documented decontamination, and unit-level testing assigned to sold units; remaining bridge value is $348,500. Do not charge the same contractor invoice again within overhead.

label: Delivery and transaction costs; value: −$41,000 | 4.0% of gross proceeds; numeric value: -41000.0; detail: Crating, insured freight, payment charges, and modeled sale-related warranty expense; remaining bridge value is $307,500. Assign warranty exposure consistently and avoid counting both the provision and settlement as separate costs.

label: Pod and operating overhead; value: −$143,500 | 14.0% of gross proceeds; numeric value: -143500.0; detail: Loaded payroll, premises, insurance, software, selling expense, and administration consume $143,500 annually, approximately $11,958 monthly within the $4,000–$18,000 canonical operating range. This is a budget envelope requiring local staffing validation.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $164,000 | Closing total, 16.0%; numeric value: 164000.0; detail: Canonical Base-Case modeled owner net, with no additional deduction invented for an unspecified tax or funding structure. Reference scenarios remain $250,000 × 10% = $25,000 and $1,800,000 × 22% = $396,000; owner net is not gross margin.

text.title: Assumptions: USD per year. First and last bars are absolute totals; the middle four bars are signed deductions. Acquisition, refurbishment, and delivery are modeled direct costs, separate from operating overhead. The cost allocation is illustrative; canonical revenue, net margin, and owner net are fixed. No unlisted residual deduction is assumed.
